title: A Study Evaluating the Antipyretic Efficacy and Safety of an Acetaminophen/Naproxen Sodium Fixed Combination in Subjects With Endotoxin-Induced Fever
official: A Randomized, Single-Dose, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study Evaluating the Antipyretic Efficacy and Safety of an Acetaminophen/Naproxen Sodium Fixed Combination in Subjects With Endotoxin-Induced Fever
summary: To evaluate the antipyretic efficacy of a single dose of a fixed combination of acetaminophen/naproxen sodium, compared with placebo.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

Subjects must meet all of the following inclusion criteria in Sections A and B to be eligible for enrollment into the study:

A) Assessed at Screening Visit (Visit 1):

1. Has a body mass index (BMI) of 17.5 to 37.0 (inclusive) for subjects who are 18 to 40 years old or a BMI of 17.5 to 35.0 (inclusive) for subjects who are 41 to 55 years old.
2. Healthy, defined as having no clinically relevant abnormalities or medical conditions identified by a detailed medical history; full physical examination; blood pressure, respiratory rate, and heart rate measurements; 12-lead ECG; and clinical laboratory tests conducted at Visit 1.
3. Has abstained from all food and drink except water at least 4 hours prior to the clinical laboratory tests at Visit 1.
4. Has a negative QuantiFERON-TB Gold Plus tuberculosis, hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C antibody, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) test based on clinical laboratory tests at Visit 1.
5. Has a negative urine drug screening test and a negative breath alcohol test conducted at Visit 1.
6. Has adequate veins, as determined by visual inspection at Visit 1, for IV catheter insertion.
7. Is able to comprehend the requirements of the study (based upon clinical site personnel's assessment) and is willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, procedures, and subject responsibilities specified within the informed consent form (ICF).
8. Has provided written informed consent before participating in any study specific procedures.
9. Agrees to follow contraception requirements (as defined in the protocol/ICF) for the duration of the study and for at least 30 days after study completion.
10. Is a non-tobacco/nicotine user or previous user who completely stopped smoking/using any form of tobacco or nicotine-containing product at least 6 months before Visit 1.

B) Assessed at Day 0 and Day 1 (of Visit 2):

1. Healthy, defined as having no clinically relevant abnormalities or medical conditions identified by a detailed medical history; full physical examination conducted on Day 0 (and symptoms-driven physical exam on Day 1, if applicable); blood pressure, respiratory rate, and heart rate measurements (conducted on Day 0 and Day 1); 12-lead ECG (conducted on Day 1), and clinical laboratory tests (conducted on Day 0).
2. Has abstained from all food and drink except water at least 4 hours prior to the clinical laboratory tests on Day 0.
3. Has a negative\* urine drug screening test and a negative breath alcohol test conducted on Day 0 (\*including a negative result for THC. A positive urine drug screening test for medications that have been prescribed to the subject are acceptable).
4. Has adequate veins, as determined by visual inspection on Day 0, for IV catheter insertion.
5. Has an oral temperature between 36.37 °C and 37.21 °C as measured on Day 0 and Day 1. If the subject's oral temperature is not between 36.37 °C and 37.21 °C after a single reading, then 2 additional oral temperature readings will be obtained within a 30-minute period. The average of these 3 consecutive temperature readings must be between 36.37 °C and 37.21 °C, with the highest value within 0.1 °C of the lowest temperature value.
6. Agrees to follow contraception requirements (as defined in the protocol/ICF) for the duration of the study and for at least 30 days after study completion.

C) Assessed Once Qualifying Fever Established (Randomization Criteria; Phase B Only) Subjects must meet all of the following criteria following endotoxin administration in order to be randomized during Phase B. Subjects who do not meet these criteria will not be randomized.

1. Has not experienced an allergic reaction or exaggerated systemic response to administration of endotoxin, as determined by the PI or medically qualified designee.
2. Has not required medical management of an AE that includes an antipyretic treatment.
3. Has developed an oral temperature of at least 38.1 ºC after endotoxin dosed per study guidelines.

Exclusion Criteria (to be assessed at Visit 1, Day 0 of Visit 2, and Day 1 of Visit 2).

Subjects must not meet any of the following exclusion criteria to be eligible for enrollment into the study

1. Has a pregnant or nursing partner or a partner who is currently trying to become pregnant.
2. Is self-reported to be unable to swallow whole large tablets or capsules.
3. Has participated in any interventional clinical studies within 30 days before Visit 1.
4. Is related to the persons involved directly or indirectly with the conduct of this study (PI, Sub-Investigator(s), study coordinators, other site personnel, employees/contractors of Kenvue or its subsidiaries, employees of IQVIA) at Visit 1.
5. Has a known allergy or hypersensitivity to acetaminophen, naproxen, naproxen sodium, ibuprofen, other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) (including acetylsalicylic acid or other salicylates), any of the inactive ingredients in the products, ondansetron, or the endotoxin used in the study.
6. Has a history of chronic tranquilizer use, heavy drinking, or substance abuse, as judged by the PI or designee, in the last five years.
7. To be assessed at Day 0: Has consumed alcohol within 48 hours prior to Day 0.
8. To be assessed at Day 0: Has consumed caffeine or other methylxanthine containing products (e.g., chocolate bars or chocolate beverages, coffee, tea, cola, or caffeinated energy drinks) within 24 hours prior to Day 0.
9. To be assessed at Day 0: Has experienced cold/flu symptoms (i.e., runny nose, cough, pain, and/or fever) within 2 weeks prior to Day 0.
10. To be assessed at Day 0: Has used prescription or nonprescription drugs within 5 half-lives prior to Day 0.
11. To be assessed at Day 0: Has used any drug that may impact gastric motility, such as glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) medication, within 35 days prior to Day 0.
12. To be assessed at Day 0: Has used vitamins or dietary/herbal supplements within 7 days prior to Day 0.
13. Routinely uses oral analgesics ≥ 5 times per week.
14. Has any disease or condition that may cause abnormal alterations in body temperature.
15. Has a clotting/bleeding disorder and is at risk of excessive bleeding.
16. Has evidence or history of a clinically significant laboratory abnormality or hematological, renal, endocrine, pulmonary, cardiovascular, hepatic, psychiatric, neurologic, immunologic, or allergic disease (excluding untreated, asymptomatic, seasonal allergies at the time of dosing) within the last 5 years that, in the PI's or medically qualified designee's opinion, may jeopardize the subject's safety or well-being or the integrity of the study.
17. Has any clinically significant gastrointestinal disorder/disease/condition or is taking medication for any such disorder/disease/condition that, per the PI's or medically qualified designee's judgement, could affect the absorption, metabolism, or excretion of the study medication.
18. Has a history of recurrent, acute, or chronic infections of any type or any findings suggestive of occult infection, such as tuberculosis, sinusitis, urinary tract infection, respiratory tract or dental (abscess) infection, etc. Also excluded are subjects with frequent (more than 3 outbreaks per year), recurrent oral or genital herpes, recurrent herpes zoster, or any infection otherwise judged by the PI or medically qualified designee to have the potential for exacerbation by participation in the study.
19. Heart rate \< 50 bpm or is deemed to be at high risk of syncope and/or hypotension per the clinical judgment of the PI or medically qualified designee at Visit 1, on Day 0, or on Day 1.
20. Supine blood pressure \<90 or \>140 mmHg (systolic) or \<50 or \>90 mmHg (diastolic), following at least 5 minutes of supine rest, as assessed at Visit 1, on Day 0, or on Day 1.
21. Supine 12-lead ECG demonstrating QTcF \>450 msec or a QRS interval \>120 msec at Visit 1 or on Day 1 prior to endotoxinadministration.
22. Other severe, acute or chronic medical or psychiatric condition(s) or laboratory abnormality(ies) that may increase the risk associated with study participation or ISM administration or may interfere with the interpretation of study results.
